work.summary: performOutbox (packages/appboundry-host/src/transactions.ts) recorded the outcome with one version-guarded put and, if that put threw, only warned and still returned next.state. Callers therefore saw 'done' or 'failed' while the record stayed 'performing'. recoverOutbox counted it as performed, and the record could later be re-run automatically after OUTBOX_PERFORMING_STALE_MS, which also breaks the rule that a failed effect is retried only by an operator. The fix: the outcome write is now tried up to OUTBOX_OUTCOME_WRITE_ATTEMPTS (3) times with a short backoff. After each failure the record is re-read. If its version moved and it is now done or failed (the write landed anyway, or another performer settled it), that persisted state is returned. If it moved but is still unsettled, or every attempt fails, the function warns and returns 'skipped' instead of reporting an outcome it never recorded. The doc comment now says 'done' and 'failed' are returned only when the record durably says so. host.ts is unchanged: 'skipped' is already part of the return type, recoverOutbox counts only 'done', and retryOutbox re-reads the record it returns. A new test, test/outbox-outcome.test.ts, uses a fake store and covers four cases: a done write that never commits (now 'skipped'), a failed write that never commits ('skipped'), a single transient write failure (retried, then 'done' with its result), and a concurrent version change ('skipped'). All 4 failed before the change and pass after it. The existing transactions and transactional-effects tests still pass, and the build passes.
